name: Gregory Boyd Penner
current_role: Chairman of Walmart Inc.; controlling owner & CEO, Denver Broncos; founder/general partner, Madrone Capital Partners
profile: Greg Penner (b. 1969), son-in-law of Rob Walton, has chaired Walmart's board since 2015 after ~20 years in Walmart roles incl. CFO of Walmart Japan. He founded Menlo Park investment firm Madrone Capital, StubHub's largest shareholder at its 2025 IPO, and leads the Walton-Penner group that bought the Denver Broncos in 2022.
interesting_fact: He is an avid mountaineer and triathlete who has summited Everest, Denali, Vinson Massif, Ama Dablam and Kilimanjaro.
deep_cut_fact: Before Walmart he was a financial analyst at Goldman Sachs and a general partner of early-stage VC fund Peninsula Capital; at Walmart he started as a store employee before rising to CFO of Walmart Japan.
notes: Walmart press office only answers working journalists. Also in April 2026 he and wife bought a 40% minority stake in the Colorado Rockies (per Wikipedia). Madrone Capital is a possible route for investment-themed outreach.

name: Guo Yingzhi
current_role: Co-founder family member of Kaisa Group (Shenzhen); reported senior advisor to Kaisa since 2015 (current status unconfirmed)
profile: Guo Yingzhi (Kwok Ying Chi) is the younger brother of Kaisa Group founder Kwok Ying Shing; the Kwok brothers held Kaisa through a family trust. He was Kaisa vice-chairman and director 2009-2014, then a senior advisor, and served as chairman/CEO of NYSE-listed Shenzhen developer Nam Tai Property from Jan 2018 to Sept 2020.
interesting_fact: After leaving Kaisa's board he was put in charge of Nam Tai Property, a former electronics maker turned Shenzhen/Wuxi property developer in which Kaisa was the largest shareholder.
notes: Very low public profile; last on Hurun 2009-2012. No personal channels found. Kaisa has been in prolonged debt restructuring, so the company is a weak route. Alive status not confirmed by any recent source.

name: Wang Bin
current_role: Founder, legal representative and CEO, Sichuan Shuyi Catering Management Co. (Shuyi Xianshaocao / 书亦烧仙草 tea chain), Chengdu
profile: Wang Bin (王斌) founded Chengdu-based tea-drink chain Shuyi Xianshaocao, which grew from one shop in 2007 to 5,200+ stores across 32 provinces plus 60+ overseas outlets. In 2022 it raised close to RMB1bn from investors including Tencent, Juewei and Qiaqia Food. In 2025 he set the slogan 'restart the business, dare to innovate' as the chain adjusts after years as China's No. 2 tea chain by scale.
interesting_fact: Shuyi's signature 'shaoxiancao' (grass-jelly) drink sold more than 200 million cups in its peak year and is still the chain's best-seller.
deep_cut_fact: The brand began in 2007 as a single shop called '85°Tea' before being renamed Shuyi Xianshaocao.
notes: Wang says he wants Shuyi to be 'the warmest and most valuable company, not the biggest' (Beijing News, Apr 2025) — a usable quote. No published press/IR email found; private company.

name: Lin Jiyong
current_role: Co-founder and co-controlling shareholder (with Wang Bingkun), De Rucci Healthy Sleep Co. (慕思股份, SZSE: 001323), Dongguan
profile: Lin Jiyong (林集永) co-founded mattress and 'healthy sleep' brand De Rucci with Wang Bingkun in Dongguan in 2004; the two are acting-in-concert controlling shareholders of the Shenzhen-listed company. De Rucci had ~4,200 stores in China by 2020 and reported 2025 revenue of RMB5.23bn.
interesting_fact: De Rucci built one of China's largest mattress retail networks (about 4,200 shops in 2020) plus showcase facilities outside China within ~16 years of founding.
notes: Very low personal profile; Wang Bingkun is the public face of De Rucci. Board secretary has since changed (Yang Nana per 2026 IR records), so verify the IR email is still monitored.

name: Liao Jieyuan
current_role: Founder and chairman, WeDoctor Group (微医, Hangzhou); left the listing-entity board in Jan 2024 but still presented as chairman in 2026
profile: Liao Jieyuan (Jerry Liao) was an early co-founder of iFlytek (1999), then ran telecom venture China Green Line before founding online hospital-booking site Guahao.com in Hangzhou in 2010, renamed WeDoctor in 2015. Backed by Tencent, Hillhouse and Sequoia China, WeDoctor refiled for a Hong Kong IPO in 2025 as an AI healthcare provider; he speaks on AI health agents.
interesting_fact: He switched to healthcare after a nephew spent ~10 months across seven hospitals with two surgeries before a misdiagnosis was found; WeDoctor's first hospital hookup (Huashan Hospital) took six months.
deep_cut_fact: Right after graduating he worked at a forestry research institute before leaving the public sector, then in 1999 helped found iFlytek with Liu Qingfeng and others.
notes: Good fit for a tech/AI angle; frequent conference speaker (World Internet Conference 2026). Dubbed one of the 'Longyan three heroes' with Zhang Yiming and Wang Xing (pedaily). 2018 interview: https://www.asianscientist.com/2018/12/features/wedoctor-jerry-liao-ai-healthcare/

name: Chen Bo
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Ningxia Jiaze Renewables Corp. (嘉泽新能, SSE: 601619); re-elected chairman of 4th board Feb 2026
profile: Chen Bo (陈波, b. 1971) built Ningxia Jiaze Renewables from Ningxia Jiaze Power Generation into a Shanghai-listed wind and solar power producer and has chaired every board since listing. Earlier he ran Beijing trading, auto-sales and aviation-services businesses. He now pitches Jiaze as an integrated new-energy power supplier and also heads Jinyuan Rongtai Investment Management (Ningxia).
interesting_fact: An energy entrepreneur directly relevant to the podcast: his company develops and operates wind and solar farms in Ningxia, northwest China, and in 2025 he described its shift toward an integrated new-energy power supplier (Shanghai Securities News interview).
deep_cut_fact: His first job was as a salesman at the Longkou Foreign Trade Company in Shandong; he later ran Beijing Yichuan Aviation Service Center before moving into wind power in Ningxia.
notes: Strong energy-podcast fit. Board secretary is now Wang Xiaoyi (appointed Feb 2026); IR email is the company's published disclosure mailbox. Many namesakes (academics) — make sure to specify Jiaze.
